title: Machine learning separates genetic salt-losing tubulopathies from other hypokalemia
summary: In 419 hypokalemic patients (291 with genetically confirmed Gitelman or Bartter syndrome) from London, Taipei and Kobe, algorithms trained on London and Taipei data were tested on the Kobe set. A decision table using serum bicarbonate and urinary sodium excretion achieved 74% accuracy, above any single biochemical variable. The authors conclude accuracy is insufficient to replace genotyping.
ai_technology: Decision table machine-learning algorithm on routine biochemistry

evidence.tested: Algorithms trained on two cohorts were tested on a third, with genotyping as reference.
evidence.unknown: Accuracy is modest; sample is from specialist clinics. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: ML algorithms identified biochemical variable combinations that distinguish salt-losing tubulopathies.
